questions.title: User Interface / Benchmarking (Question 21, CSSA 2024)

items.text:
When designing a user interface, many factors must be considered by a developer.   Two of these factors are: 

  • recognition of relevant social and ethical issues 

  • current common practice in interface design 

 Describe TWO other factors that should be considered by the developer in the user interface design process.

criteria.criterion: Describes TWO factors thoroughly
Outlines TWO factors OR describes ONE factor
Shows some understanding of factors to be considered

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Factors to be addressed with a good description could include:

  • consideration of the intended audience

  • identification of screen size

  • identification of data fields and screen elements required and their appropriate on-screen placement

  • online help

  • consistency in approach

items.text:
A retailer of pet products employed a software developer to create a website for online marketing of their broad range of products. 

They have considered using either the Prototyping approach or the Agile approach for the development.

Explain how benchmarking could be used when testing the website.

criteria.criterion: Provides an excellent description of the benchmarking process and the testing of measurable quality assurance requirements
Outlines some features of the benchmarking process
Shows some understanding of benchmarking as a quality assurance testing process

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Benchmarking is an essential part of quality assurance. It relies on strict and measurable criteria being set during the requirements phase and it is used to test that the software meets the pre-defined quality requirements.

These criteria are tested during each stage of production to ensure that the final product meets or exceeds the requirements. In this website example the criteria could include speed of loading under different conditions or its ability to handle volume requests without failing.

Sometimes a product will be benchmarked against a similar product so that a comparison can be made between them.

questions.title: Feasibility analysis, development approach, and modelling tools in software planning (Q21, CSSA 2017)

items.text:
‘Splashes’ is a family owned business which provides swimming lessons for all ages. They are currently using a paper-based system to manage all their clients, instructors, bookings and payments.

An example of a running day for them includes: 4 sessions per day (level 1, level 2, level 3 and level 4) each running for 30 minutes each. A client arrives and informs them of their child’s name and the receptionist looks for the child’s card/file from a filing system which is then manually ticked off against the correct date to confirm attendance and payment. If a child is absent, a cross is placed next to their name. The client then pays a fee of $15 for the lesson. If a child is absent, they are still required to pay for missed lesson(s) the following week and book in for a catch up lesson(s).

The business owner has realised that this manual system is not effective and costing her money due to human error. The owner wishes to invest in a new computer-based system to overcome these issues.
Explain the factors that should be considered by a software developer prior to investing time and money into a proposed software solution.

criteria.criterion: Provides a clear explanation of the factors to be considered
Provides explanation of a factor OR identifies factors to be considered
Identifies a factor

questions.title: Implementation of Software Solutions (Question 24, ITE 2014)

items.text:
The Drama department at ABC High School wishes to develop a database allowing them to catalogue their vast costume and props collection. The Head of Drama has suggested that the staff use DataMaker Pro – a database package which provides a visual interface to design the database schema and user interface to input the required information.

The database must allow for the input and storage of the following information:

  • Name of the item (e.g. red dress, foam block, lighting rig).
  • Category – selectable from the following list: costume, prop, equipment.
  • Location – selectable from the following list: equipment store, costume rack A, costume rack B, costume rack C, prop shelf A, prop shelf B, prop shelf C.
  • Description – free text input.
  • Photo of the item.

During the development of the database it became apparent that some complex code and database queries had to be implemented. The Drama staff did not have the level of knowledge to write these themselves, so they managed to find the required code on an internet forum. As a result, they have included this code in their database program.

Discuss the social and ethical implications of including this code from the internet.

criteria.criterion: Discusses social and ethical implications, showing a good understanding of the issues involved and the given scenario.
Discusses social and ethical implications.
Identifies a relevant issue.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
• Plagiarism. The teachers should acknowledge the source of the code in the comments. They
    also need to consider the source of the code – did the person who posted it on the forum write the code? What do the terms and conditions of the forum say about the use of code found on the
    forum?

  • Quality. How will the teachers know if the code they are sourcing from the forum is of good
    quality? Does it have any unintended consequences for the database program or the system on which it is used?

items.text: Design an appropriate screen for the entry of new items into the database.

criteria.criterion: Provides a screen design showing a good understanding of screen design principles and screen elements.
Provides a screen design with appropriate screen elements.
Provides a screen design relevant to the scenario.

items.text: The Head of Drama would like the database to be accessible to all staff via the school network. Describe TWO aspects they should consider given that the software will be accessible over a network.

criteria.criterion: Describes two aspects to be considered, showing a good understanding of the scenario and network access of software.
Describes an aspect to be considered.
Identifies an aspect to be considered.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
• Licencing. Is the school licenced to use DataMaker Pro on all staff computers? This would need to be checked and additional licences or a site licence purchased if necessary.

  • Installation of DataMaker Pro. Is DataMaker Pro currently installed on all staff computers? If
    not, someone will need to install it. Individual software installations is a time-consuming and
    labour-intensive process. Whether the installation of DataMaker Pro can be automated should beinvestigated.

  • Storage of database. Where will the data file reside? In a single-user database the data file
    often resides on the hard drive of the person using the database. If multiple users are using the database simultaneously then the database needs to be stored on the network. This has issues for licencing, for speed of access, and for the technical difficulties associated with simultaneous access to a database. For example, what happens if two users try to simultaneously access or update a record?

  • Speed of access. If the data file is stored on the network then access to the database will take longer. If the photos of the items are stored in high-resolution then there may be delays in accessing and displaying the data, particularly over wireless connections where the coverage could be patchy and the speeds slow.

items.text: The software will continue to be developed with new features over time. Outline how software version control tools could be used to help manage these changes.

criteria.criterion: Shows an understanding of the features of software version control tools and the scenario.
Shows an understanding of the features of software version control tools.
Identifies a relevant feature.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
• Keeping backups of old versions. Software version control tools usually keep backups of old
    versions of software. If a problem was to develop with the costumes and props database, then the staff could roll back the database to an earlier version. Ideally the database program itself (consisting of the schema and forms) will be separate to the data file (consisting of the photos and details of costumes and props), so that a roll-back of the database will not lose information about costumes and props.

  • Keeping track of when changes were made, who made them, and why there were made.
    This information is invaluable in case an error is found in the database (it can be traced back to when it occurred), or to get further information about why a change to the database was made.

questions.title: Developer Responsibility for Quality and Information Accuracy in Software (Question 22, ITE 2021)

items.text:
Consider the following news article:

Facebook could have prevented billions of views on pages that shared misinformation related to the 2020 U.S. election, according to a new report released Tuesday, which slams the platform for “creating the conditions that swept America down the dark path from election to insurrection.”

The report, by the online advocacy group Avaaz, found that if Facebook had not waited until October to tweak its algorithms to stem false and toxic content amplified on the platform, the company could have prevented an estimated 10.1 billion views on the 100 most prominent pages that repeatedly shared misinformation on the platform ahead of the election.

- Time Magazine, 23 March 2021

Discuss the responsibilities of software developers to build quality software and also ensure that information contained in their software is accurate. Refer to the above news article in your response.

criteria.criterion: Discusses the responsibility of software developers to build quality solutions AND ensure information in their software is accurate including reference to the Facebook quotation.
Discusses the responsibility of software developers to build quality solutions OR ensure information in their software is accurate.
Identifies a responsibility of software developers.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Software developers have the responsibility to build quality software which meets customer expectations and requirements. For example, Facebook has the responsibility to build a platform which provides the user with the advertised service - in this case, the ability to see and read updates from friends and family along with providing news.

As part of providing a quality product, there is an expectation that the information contained in the software is accurate and correct. Whilst it is difficult to achieve this when much of the content in the product is being provided by third-parties (in this example, news websites) the developer does have a responsibility to ensure that the algorithms within their software do their best to promote accurate and reliable information - since that is something which is an expectation of their service.

questions.title: Data structures and sorting algorithms for contact and date management (Q23, CSSA 2017)

items.text:
A computer programmer keeps a list of his contacts in a sorted table. As he does not add to this list of contacts very often, he keeps any new entries in an unsorted overflow table. When he needs to find a contact he performs a binary search on the sorted table and if the contact is still not found, he looks up the overflow table using a linear search.

Describe an advantage and a disadvantage of using this method.

criteria.criterion: Clearly describes advantage and disadvantage of method used
Describe an advantage or disadvantage
Identifies an advantage or disadvantage

items.text:
The Extract(Start, Finish, DataString) subprogram copies the characters from the Start value to the Finish value from DataString.

Construct an algorithm in pseudocode that will convert a date string formatted as

"MM/DD/YYYY" into a format of "DD/MM/YYYY".

criteria.criterion: Provides a substantially correct algorithm
Provides a mostly correct algorithm
Constructs a partially correct algorithm
Attempts an algorithm

items.text:
The following algorithm sorts an array of names into ascending order.

 

BEGIN BubbleSort  

 Let Last = number of names in the array  

Let Swapped = true  

WHILE Swapped = true  

Let Swapped = false  

Let i = 1  

WHILE i < Last  

IF Name (i) > Name (i+1) THEN

Swap (Name (i), Name (i+1))

Let Swapped = true

ENDIF  

 Increment i  

 ENDWHILE  

 Decrement Last  

 ENDWHILE  

END BubbleSort 

 

 

Write the Swap subprogram that could be used for the above example.

criteria.criterion: Writes a correct Swap algorithm
Writes a partially correct algorithm

items.text:
Tickets for international superstar Yat Yat Fast are on sale for her tour of Australia. All tickets are General Admission (GA).

An integer would be used for the total number of tickets purchased.

BEGIN Main  

GET NumberofTickets  

GET TicketType

questions.title: Data Structures and Writing Algorithms for Athlete Performance Processing (Question 26, ITE 2023)

items.text:
There is a large 400 metre running festival with three races over three days. The first two races have all athletes commencing together, but the final race will be a "chasing start", meaning athletes are handicapped based on their results in the previous races.

The handicap for the chasing start is determined by averaging each athlete’s previous two race times, with competitors starting in descending order of their average time. The runner with the slowest/highest average time starts first with each faster runner beginning in turn.

Consider the following sample data. In reality there will be many more athletes.

Surname

FirstName

Race1

Race2

Average

Handicap

Johnson

Emily

52.56

52.255

46.25

Sophia Williams starts first in the final race as her average time for the first 2 races is slowest/highest. Ethan starts second 0.815 seconds later because his average time is 0.815 seconds faster than Sophia. Benjamin Hayes, who has the fastest average time, starts last in the final race and begins 7.18 seconds after Sophia.
Recommend and justify data structures for storing the data both during processing and permanently.

criteria.criterion: Recommends and justifies an appropriate data structure for use during processing AND persistent storage.
Recommends and justifies an appropriate data structure for use during processing OR persistent storage
Identifies an appropriate data structure for use during processing AND persistent storage.
Identifies an appropriate data structure for use during processing OR persistent storage

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
During processing, an appropriate data structure would be an array of records. This is appropriate because each runner has a group of related data, in different data types, which needs to be stored together: surname, firstname, race 1 time, race 2 time, average, and handicap. Then, each of these records can be stored in an array so they can collectively be accessible from a single data structure.

To store the data persistently, a relative file would be most appropriate. As the data is being stored in records they are a perfect use-case for relative files, as each record has the same number of fields each with a fixed size. This also means that each record could be accessed individually without having to read the entire file contents into memory, which is useful if the data for a single runner needs to be retrieved in the software.

items.text: Write an algorithm to calculate the Average of the first two race times for each athlete. You may assume the Surname, FirstName and results of Race1 and Race2 have already been entered.

criteria.criterion:
Provides a substantially correct algorithm, including all of the following:

  • Loop to iterate over each competitor
  • Correctly retrieves the current competitor on each iteration of the loop
  • Calculates the average of the Race1 and Race2 times for the competitor
  • Appropriately displays or stores the average

Provides an algorithm, including some of the following:

  • Loop to iterate over each competitor
  • Correctly retrieves the current competitor on each iteration of the loop
  • Calculates the average of the Race1 and Race2 times for the competitor
  • Appropriately displays or stores the average
An attempt at an algorithm to meet the requirements.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
BEGIN CalculateAverages(Competitor)

MaxIndex = Maximum index in array Competitor

FOR i = 0 TO MaxIndex-1 STEP 1

Competitor[i].Average = (Competitor[i].Race1 + Competitor[i].Race2) / 2

NEXT i

END

Note: Assumes the array Competitor is indexed from 0

items.text: Write an algorithm to calculate the Handicap for each athlete in the final race. You may assume the averages from part (b) above have already been calculated.

criteria.criterion:
Provides a substantially correct algorithm, including all of the following:

  • Determines the highest average time either by sorting or searching
  • Loops through all competitors to calculate handicaps
  • Correctly calculates the handicap time for each competitor

Provides a substantially correct algorithm, including all of the following:

  • Determines the highest average time either by sorting or searching with minor error
  • Loops through all competitors to calculate handicaps
  • Correctly calculates the handicap time for each competitor

Provides an algorithm, including some of the following:

  • Determines the highest average time either by sorting or searching with errors
  • Loops through all competitors to calculate handicaps
  • Correctly calculates the handicap time for each competitor

Provides an algorithm, including at least TWO of the following:

  • Determines the highest average time either by sorting or searching with errors
  • Loops through all competitors to calculate handicaps
  • Correctly calculates the handicap time for each competitor

Provides an algorithm, including a genuine attempt to perform TWO of the following but with errors:

  • Determines the highest average time either by sorting or searching
  • Loops through all competitors to calculate handicaps
  • Correctly calculates the handicap time for each competitor
An attempt at an algorithm to address the requirements.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Note: searching for the highest time without the need to sort is the most efficient solution. Teachers may like to only give full marks for solutions utilising a search, subtracting a mark when a sort is described. Suggested answers for both search and sort-based solutions are provided.

BEGIN CalculateHandicapsWithSearch(Competitor)

// Find highest average time

MaxIndex = Maximum index in array Competitor

Highest = 0

FOR i = 0 to MaxIndex STEP 1

IF Competitor[i].Average > Highest THEN

Highest = Competitor[i].Average

END IF

NEXT i

// Calculate handicap and start order

FOR i = 0 TO MaxIndex STEP 1

Competitor[i].Handicap = Highest - Competitor[i].Average

NEXT i

END

 

BEGIN CalculateHandicapsWithSort(Competitor)

// Sort competitors ascending by average time using bubble sort

MaxIndex = Maximum index in array Competitor

Last = MaxIndex

Swapped = True

WHILE Swapped = True

Swapped = False

i = 0

WHILE i < Last

IF Competitor[i].Average > Competitor[i + 1].Average THEN

Temp = CompetitorArray[i]

Competitor[i] = Competitor[i + 1]

CompetitorArray[i + 1] = Temp

Swapped = True

END IF

i = i + 1

END WHILE

Last = Last - 1

END WHILE

// Calculate handicap

FOR i = 0 TO MaxIndex STEP 1

Competitor[i].Handicap = Competitor[MaxIndex].Average - Competitor[i].Average

NEXT i

END

Note: Assumes the array is indexed from 0

questions.title: Data Type Selection and the Year 2038 Problem (Question 21, ITE 2021)

items.text:
The Unix timestamp is a way to keep track of time on computers. It represents the current time as the number of seconds since midnight on 1 January 1970.

Some computer programs store the Unix timestamp in a 32-bit integer. However, in the year 2038 the Unix timestamp will grow to be a larger number than a 32-bit integer can store. This is known as the Year 2038 Problem.

Discuss an implication for software developers when selecting appropriate data types for use in their programs with reference to the Year 2038 Problem.

criteria.criterion: Discusses ONE implication when selecting appropriate data types with reference to the scenario.
Discusses ONE implication when selecting appropriate data types.
Identifies an implication when selecting appropriate data types.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
• Developers should consider future possible implications of the data types they select. In the case of the Year 2038 Problem, software developers chose a data type which did not have sufficient expandability into the future - likely because the year 2038 was considered a long time away and software would have been upgraded to support larger dates by that time.

  • Developers should test their programs with large inputs. During the testing phase of their software the developers may have tested the program with smaller date inputs which fall into the range of a 32-bit integer, neglecting to test with larger inputs which exceed that storage capacity.

items.text: Recommend and justify a suitable paradigm to use for the development of this railway network application.

criteria.criterion:
Provides a suitable recommendation and justification for use of a particular paradigm, with
reference to the network rail application.
Provides a suitable recommendation and justification for use of a particular paradigm.
Identifies features of a particular paradigm.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
The problem of finding the shortest route between stations (also known as the least-cost route in graph based problems) can be solved through writing an algorithm. There are several established algorithms to solve this problem, including Dijkstra’s algorithm. However, these often do require the representation of the graph using particular data types. Therefore, it is recommended that an object-oriented paradigm be used in the development of this application. It has all the advantages and features of a purely imperative approach, but also adds support for objects and complex data types which may need to be used to represent nodes in the graph (i.e. stations) and the interrelationship between those nodes (i.e. links between stations).
(Note: students may choose any paradigm, it is their justification that is critical)

items.text:
Describe how inheritance helps to improve the productivity of programmers.

Provide a specific example of inheritance to illustrate your answer.

criteria.criterion: Describes how inheritance can improve the productivity of programmers, including examples.
Describes how inheritance can improve the productivity of programmers.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Inheritance helps improve the productivity of programmers in the following ways:

  • Reducing the amount of code to write (or rewrite). If a superclass can be written which contains generic behaviour then using inheritance the programmer can create subclasses which inherit that generic behaviour but can also extend and supplement that with their own behaviour specific to the subclass. For example, a superclass may be Car which defines all the generic aspects of a car (e.g. manufacturer, model, colour). Then, the developer could implement subclasses for different types of cars with specific behaviours. For example, FourWheelDrive which includes information about whether the vehicle as a diff lock. This saves the developer from having to rewrite and duplicate all the generic Car code in all classes which they write.

  • Reduces scope for errors. More code generally results in more scope and opportunity for errors. Using inheritance the developer can reduce the amount of code they need to write (particularly, code duplication) as discussed in the previous point. This means there is less scope for error to occur since less code is being written.

  • Reusability of classes. Using inheritance potentially allows classes to be reused in many different programs, and extended as needed. For example, the generic Car class could be used in many different programs, with each program subclassing Car to add their own custom implementation of subclasses.

questions.title: Design, Privacy, and Development Strategy for a Contact Tracing App (Question 27, ITE 2020)

items.text:
In response to a virus pandemic, the government is developing an app called TrialSafe. The app will assist health authorities in contacting people who have been in close contact with people with the virus.

The key features of the TrialSafe app are:

  • Users are invited to install it on their smartphones

  • Users provide their phone number, age group and postcode during registration

  • During registration the health department provides a unique ID to the user, which is stored on their phone.

  • During use the app collects IDs from other smartphone users with the app who are nearby

  • If a user tests positive to the virus, they are invited to upload the collected IDs to the health department. A confirmation message is provided to the user once the upload has completed successfully.

The development team have a three week timeline to develop the app.

A context diagram is shown below.
Draw a Data Flow Diagram based on the key features of the TrialSafe app.

criteria.criterion:
A correct DFD with the following features
● 3 nominated external entities
● at least 3 processes
● a data store
● correct internal and external data flows
Provides a DFD with some appropriate processes and showing some understanding of the system
Provides some DFD symbols showing some understanding of the system
A modelling tool showing some understanding of the system

items.text: Describe privacy issues which may arise from the TrialSafe app.

criteria.criterion: Describes relevant privacy considerations, showing a good understanding of privacy and the scenario.
Identifies a relevant privacy consideration.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
An important privacy principle is the protection of a person’s data and identity. The TrialSafe app does not collect names, but it should ensure that the phone numbers, postcodes and age ranges stored by the Health Department should be stored securely and only necessary staff should have access. 

Exchanging IDs rather than names or phone numbers also ensures the privacy of users, but it is important that the database matching IDs to phone numbers is also kept secure.

The privacy policy should be provided to users so that they know exactly how the data is used and
stored.

items.text: Recommend and justify a software development approach for this app.

criteria.criterion: Recommends an appropriate approach, and provides a justification that shows understanding of the approach and the scenario.
Recommends an approach, and provides a justification that shows understanding of the approach or the scenario.
Identifies an approach.

markingRubricContentItem.text: The three week timeline is a big constraint on the development team, so Agile is most appropriate. This will allow a working version of the program to be delivered reasonably quickly, and bugs can then be fixed and new versions released regularly. There are some complexities in this program, such as ensuring the app works on a wide range of devices and that the ID exchange works correctly and reliably. An agile approach means that over time more devices can be tested and the program modified to ensure they work correctly.

questions.title: Discuss the implications for both XYZ Software and the company's customers of this change (Question 24, ITE 2023)

items.text:
XYZ Software developed a word processor software package. Until 2015, they sold it as a standalone product called XYZ Document, only requiring users to make a single up-front payment. After 2015, they stopped selling the standalone product and moved to a software as a service model. Their new word processor called XYZ Docs is only available online as a web app using a subscription-based pricing model where users need to pay a yearly fee to keep access to the software.

Recently, XYZ Software said they are creating a new file format for XYZ Docs which will not be supported by XYZ Document. Any users who are still using the XYZ Document will need to change to the new online, subscription-based software to maintain interoperability with the new software.
Discuss the implications for both XYZ Software and the company's customers of this change.

criteria.criterion: Discusses implications for BOTH XYZ Software AND the customer's of the software.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:

questions.title: Software Development Responsibilities, Licensing, Installation and Quality Assurance (Question 24, ITE 2022)

items.text: A software developer has been engaged by a small manufacturing business to write custom software. The software will manage safety compliance on a production line and is required before a new law comes into effect in two months.

A responsibility of software developers is the regular backup of their work.

What are the implications for the developer and client if this did not occur?

criteria.criterion: Provides a detailed explanation of the implications for the software developer AND the client.
Provides some explanation of the implications for the software developer AND the client
Provides some explanation of the implications for the software developer OR the client.
Identifies an implication for the software developer OR the client.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Implications for the developer:

  • Should an event occur which results in loss of work, such as a hard drive crash, then the developer would still be held liable to produce the output as required by the contract with the business. This could put them under significant pressure, in terms of both resourcing and finances (e.g. paying their staff overtime), to deliver on the contract requirements if they have to re-do the lost work.
  • If there is accidental deletion of work, or perhaps work needs to be reverted to a previous version due to the introduction of errors, it would be difficult to recover previous versions if no regular backups are available allowing the work to be reverted to a particular point in time.

Implications for the client:

  • If work is lost, due to the developer not backing up the work, then this may result in the system not being ready within the required time frame of two months. The client may be put into a difficult position since the software is required for them to comply with new legislation.
  • Following from the previous point, the client is likely to need the software complete within the two month time frame regardless - so they may be forced to pay extra for additional resources (such as programmers) to make up for lost time and lost work.

items.text:
The developer would like to sell the finished software to other businesses. 

Discuss the copyright and licencing implications.

criteria.criterion: Provides a comprehensive discussion of the copyright and licensing issues.
Provides some discussion of the copyright and licensing issues.
Identifies a copyright or licensing issue.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
In Australia, the default position is that copyrights/IP remains with the author, in this case the developer. The opposite default position is the case for software developed in a number of other countries including the USA.

In Australia, often, and in particular for custom products the contract provides that the copyrights/IP are to be assigned to the client. Therefore, licensing and resale very much depends on the conditions of the contract between the developer and the client. 

If no contract reassigning copyrights to the client exists, then the developer owns the copyrights/IP and is free to sell and license as they wish.

If the contract specifies copyright is owned by the client rather than the developer then the developer could not sell the software. However, they may be able to negotiate an agreement with the client to license the software for resale. Additionally, if the client owns copyright the developer would also be unable to reuse any of the source code or proprietary algorithms which were written for the client in other software which they may write for themselves or other clients in the future. This would also be classified as a breach of copyright.

This method of installation would also reduce risk significantly, compared with alternative approaches such as direct cut-over, where if the new software fails the entire system it supports is non-functional.

Given the critical nature of this software, that it is needed to meet a legislative requirement, quality assurance practices can be used to ensure processes and criteria are put in place during the software development to ensure high standards are met. Some quality assurance practices may include:

  • The establishment of measurable metrics and criteria upon which the software can be objectively evaluated throughout the development process and also at the end deliverable stage.
  • Using a version control system, to allow for the coordinated management of source code during development.
  • Regular code reviews and peer reviews, which can help identify errors or bugs in coding during the early development stages while also allowing developers to see each other's code to adhere to consistent development practices (e.g. naming conventions, comment quality, etc.).

questions.title: Implementing Quality Assurance Across the Software Development Cycle (Question 26, ITE 2021)

items.text:
The five stages of the software development cycle are: 

  • defining and understanding the problem, 

  • planning and designing software solutions, 

  • implementation of software solutions, 

  • testing and evaluating software solutions, and 

  • maintaining software solutions.

Describe how a quality assurance process can be implemented throughout all stages of the software development cycle.

criteria.criterion: Thoroughly describes how a quality assurance process can be implemented in all FIVE stages of the software development cycle.
Describes how a quality assurance process can be implemented in at least FOUR stages of the software development cycle.
Describes how a quality assurance process can be implemented in at least THREE stages of the software development cycle.
Describes how a quality assurance process can be implemented in at least TWO stages of the software development cycle.
Identifies features of quality assurance.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
• Defining and understanding the problem. The criteria which the software quality will be evaluated against should be established. Aspects of quality software such as correctness, reliability, efficiency, integrity, usability, etc. should be considered when developing the criteria.

  • Planning and designing software solutions. The criteria established in the previous stage should be referenced to ensure that the design of the software solution will meet that criteria. If any issues are identified then it will be easier to solve them at this point rather than after the software has been implemented.

  • Implementation of software solutions. Following the plan devised in the previous stage to develop the software. Ideally, the software plan will have considered the quality assurance criteria so if the plan is followed the software should be implemented to meet that criteria. If there are any changes during implementation then the criteria should be referenced to ensure that the software product still meets those requirements.

  • Testing and evaluating software solutions. This will involve testing the software and evaluating it against the criteria which was established in the first stage (defining and understanding the problem) to ensure that it meets or exceeds those criteria.

  • Maintaining software solutions. Whenever maintenance is conducted on the software the original software quality criteria should be referenced to ensure that the modifications meet those criteria. This would also be evaluated when the modifications go through the testing phase.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Sign and modulus

Sign bit 1, followed by 000 0110 for 6 (2+4), i.e. 1000 0110

1s complement

The first bit is the sign bit.

items.text:
A number is represented in single precision floating point form as follows.

1 10000011 10111100000000000000000

What decimal number is represented?

criteria.criterion: Correct answer
Working shows understanding of two components
Shows some understanding of floating point representation

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Sign bit is 1, so it is a negative number

Stored exponent is 10000011, i.e. 131.

The actual exponent is 131-127=4

The mantissa is 101111

So our number is (starting with a minus sign and the hidden bit) -1.101111 * 24

Shifting the binary point 4 places to the right gives us -11011.11

Then converting to decimal:

= -(16+8+2+1+0.5+0.25)

= -27.75

items.text:

In your response:

  • Outline the key characteristics of each approach.

  • Discuss one advantage and one disadvantage of each.

  • Justify a project scenario where pure Agile would be more suitable than Wagile.

criteria.criterion:
Clear, accurate description of both Wagile (hybrid planning + iteration) and Agile (fully iterative, feedback-driven).

One valid advantage and disadvantage for each approach.

Specific scenario with logical justification for why Agile suits it better (e.g., changing requirements in startups).

Provides a satisfactory scenario and attempts to justify why Agile suits it better.

Some valid advantages and disadvantages for both approaches, OR

Provides a satisfactory scenario and attempts to justify why Agile suits it better.

Any two of the following:

  • Identifies only advantages or disadvantages, or covers just one approach, OR

  • Describes only one approach correctly, OR

  • Identifies a scenario but lacks justification

Any one of the following:

  • Identifies only advantages or disadvantages, or covers just one methodology, OR

  • Describes only one methodology correctly, OR

  • Identifies a scenario but lacks justification

markingGuidanceContentItem.text:
Wagile blends Waterfall's structured planning with Agile's iterative delivery. It begins with upfront requirements gathering (like Waterfall) but implements features in sprints (like Agile), allowing some flexibility while maintaining project milestones.

Pure Agile is fully iterative, focusing on delivering working software in short cycles through continuous customer collaboration. It prioritises responding to change over following a fixed plan, with less upfront documentation.

Wagile’s advantage: balances predictability (from Waterfall) with adaptability (from Agile), suitable for projects needing clear timelines but some flexibility. Wagile’s disadvantage: can be inefficient if initial plans require frequent revisions, leading to delays.

Agile’s advantage: excels in dynamic environments due to rapid response to feedback. Agile’s disadvantage: risk of scope creep without rigid deadlines, potentially increasing costs.

One scenario where pure Agile would be more suitable: A mobile app startup developing a fitness tracker. With the Agile approach, short sprint reviews (e.g. weekly) to incorporate user feedback on features like heart-rate monitoring. However, Wagile’s upfront design phase might delay these adjustments. For example, if beta testers request a sleep-tracking feature, Agile teams can add it in the next sprint, while Wagile would require revisiting initial plans.

questions.title: Recommending a software development approach for a high-risk, long-term automation project (Q23, CSSA 2015)

items.text:
A mining company wants Nick Industries to design software, to control its fleet of robot explorers. After the requirements phase the mining company doesn’t have the time or resources to be involved in the project other than reviews, approvals and status meetings. The software doesn’t have to be developed quickly as it is a long term project. It is important that the software is fully tested as the robot hardware is very expensive and easily damaged if not controlled correctly.

Compare TWO suitable software development approaches Nick Industries could use to design the software and recommend the most appropriate software development approach for this scenario.

criteria.criterion: Shows a clear understanding of a Structured approach and another suitable approach and selects the Structured approach as being the most appropriate for this scenario
Shows a clear understanding of a Structured approach and  another suitable approach
Shows an understanding of a Structured approach and  another suitable approach and
Shows an understanding of two approaches
Identifies two approaches

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Structured approach

• Developers and customers agree on what will be delivered early in the development lifecycle. This makes planning and designing more straightforward.

• Progress is more easily measured, as the full scope of the work is known in advance.

• Throughout the development effort, it’s possible for various members of the team to be involved or to continue with other work, depending on the active phase of the project. For example, business analysts can learn about and document what needs to be done, while the developers are working on other projects. Testers can prepare test scripts from requirements documentation while coding is underway.

• Except for reviews, approvals, status meetings, etc., a customer presence is not strictly required after the requirements phase.

• Because design is completed early in the development lifecycle, this approach lends itself to projects where multiple software components must be designed (sometimes in parallel) for integration with external systems.  

• Finally, the software can be designed completely and more carefully, based upon a more complete understanding of all software deliverables. This provides a better software design with less likelihood of the “piecemeal effect,” a development phenomenon that can occur as pieces of code are defined and subsequently added to an application where they may or may not fit well.

 

Agile approach

Agile is an iterative, team-based approach to development. This approach emphasizes the rapid delivery of an application in complete functional components.

• The customer has frequent and early opportunities to see the work being delivered, and to make decisions and changes throughout the development project.

• The customer gains a strong sense of ownership by working extensively and directly with the project team throughout the project.

• If time to market for a specific application is a concern, Agile can more quickly produce a basic version of working software.

• Development is often more user-focused, likely a result of more and frequent direction from the customer

 

Students could also discuss

– Prototyping, RAD, End user approaches

questions.title: Express the decimal number –29 in 8 bit binary, using each of the following  systems. Show all working.  Sign and modulus  2’s complement (Q35, ITE 2017)

items.text:
Express the decimal number –29 in 8 bit binary, using each of the following

systems. Show all working.

  1. Sign and modulus
  2.  2’s complement

criteria.criterion: Correct answer with all relevant working for both parts
Almost correct answer but with some errors or omissions

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
I. Sign and modulus:

29 = 16 + 8 + 4 + 1

= 00011101 in binary

But -29 is negative, so the sign bit (the leftmost bit) must be a 1

= 10011101

II. 29 = 00011101 in binary (as above)

To form its 2’s complement, we flip the bits and add 1

= 11100010 + 1

= 11100011
